recommended_title: Variance-Guided Benchmark Selection with Masked Low-Rank Score Models
central_question: Under limited benchmark-query budgets, how well does variance-guided selection with masked low-rank reconstruction predict held-out models' remaining observed scores across model-disjoint and name-family-disjoint leaderboard splits?
central_thesis: On the two pinned leaderboard matrices, the retained variance-guided low-rank method has a higher pooled remaining-target prediction score than the tested baselines and loses score under historical-column derangement, supporting a conditional empirical result rather than universal benchmark sufficiency, response-adaptive selection, or fixed-target superiority.
narrative_rationale: The strongest evidence is the sealed final comparison of one retained method against five operational baselines across two sources, two split regimes, and three seeds, with a paired uncertainty interval against random-query low-rank prediction and a dependence-destroying control. Present MTEB embedding tasks and Open LLM generative-model benchmarks as separate evidence blocks under a shared score-matrix question; fit each source independently, without cross-source model alignment or transfer claims. The contribution is a transparent empirical assessment and reproducible mechanism description, not a newly discovered winning architecture. The alternatives have no measured performance evidence. The informative limitations, especially method-dependent remaining targets and non-response-adaptive selection, belong in the central argument rather than only in the supplement.
edit_framing_decision: Fresh framing, not an edit: no resolved edit-context files, previous_paper manuscript, aggregated directory, or extra_tasks directory are staged. The status 'rejected' records that no inherited manuscript story is adopted; it does not reject a scientific result. Preserve-with-local-updates has no prior manuscript to preserve; broaden-to-a-shared-method-family is unsupported for the unscored alternative implementations; recenter-on-the-retained-evaluated-method is selected because it has direct final evidence. No old title or figure plan is carried forward.
staged_input_impact: Direct inspection of source_evidence/downstream/program/src/program.py establishes masked alternating ridge factors, historical-cell rank selection, conditional ridge reconstruction, and set-conditioned variance-reduction querying; purchased values affect prediction but not query choice.

The staged selected and original-baseline source files are byte-identical. Study selection is the original baseline, not an improved search winner; do not manufacture a second final comparator for the same source.

The final evidence supplies the actual scientific comparison despite the absence of scored search alternatives. The final qualification record is read independently of the downstream selection summary.

The pinned final audit, plan, task contract, and evaluator's scoring/baseline definitions explain the two data domains, remaining-target score, heuristic family grouping, budgets, and bootstrap semantics. They are protocol provenance, not additional experimental results or substitute quantitative grounding IDs.

The current bibliography/provenance contains retrieved factorization-related metadata but lacks the permitted starter and dataset records needed for domain positioning. This limits literature claims, not the coherence of the measured comparison; the writer must verify relevant allowed records before citing them and must not fill pages with unrelated retrieval hits. No network retrieval is performed in this framing stage.

method_groups.name: Variance-guided masked low-rank reconstruction
method_groups.include_reason: The single studied method. Describe 'proposed' only as the contract role, not a novelty or search-improvement claim. The retained source learns masked factors and selects queries using a conditional trace-reduction proxy. Ground performance in final.evidence.episodes and final.metric.combined_score.

method_groups.name: Random-query masked low-rank reconstruction
method_groups.include_reason: The closest selector comparison: source inspection confirms the same factor-fitting and prediction construction with random available queries. A pooled paired family-clustered interval is available against this comparator; different remaining targets still prevent a fixed-target causal interpretation.

method_groups.name: Information-selected covariance ridge
method_groups.include_reason: Strongest pooled nonfactor comparator. It changes representation, regularization selection, and potentially query sets, so it is a joint pipeline comparison rather than a matched-query reconstruction ablation. Retain the Open LLM family-split seed where it slightly exceeds the studied method.

method_groups.name: Correlation-medoid covariance ridge
method_groups.include_reason: Tests a simpler correlation-centrality query ordering with covariance reconstruction; provides an interpretable selection comparator without adding an unevaluated method family.

method_groups.name: Historical benchmark means
method_groups.include_reason: Observation-invariant reference for the substantial predictability already present in historical task means. Its operational score is computed on its own query-policy remainder, not a universal zero-query target set.

method_groups.name: Random-query mean-offset prediction
method_groups.include_reason: Simple purchased-score reference: shift historical benchmark means by the observed mean residual. Distinguishes structured reconstruction from a global model-level offset.

results_focus: Primary view: final noncontrol, nonreplay case scores for the six methods, stratified by source and split, with all three seed observations visible. Label the metric 'Normalized prediction score (1 - MAE; higher is better)', not percent accuracy or variance explained. Average only with the documented equal target/row/checkpoint/seed/split/source hierarchy.

Pooled evidence: studied method 0.9527636891226994, random-query low-rank 0.9364101694132948, information-selected ridge 0.9482262260487015, medoid ridge 0.9327472829724573, mean-offset 0.920605668187274, and historical means 0.90687688776656. Use a compact table, not a redundant figure. Only the studied-versus-random-low-rank comparison has a supplied paired interval: [0.014807167765235746, 0.01847801943997085]. Do not attach that interval to another comparator or a source/split cell.

Source evidence remains distinct: MTEB pooled score 0.9468974985138557 and Open LLM pooled score 0.9586298797315429 describe different task and budget regimes, not a controlled difficulty comparison. MTEB is embedding-model evidence, not evidence about generative LLM benchmark suites.

Dependence control: compare actual and independently column-deranged historical training scores for each source/split with paired seeds; pooled deranged score 0.9233917542059907 and actual-minus-deranged score 0.029371934916708625. The control supports dependence on historical alignment, not unique causal attribution to the acquisition rule or immunity to leakage.

Qualification for claims: the factor method is not best in every retained cell. In Open LLM family split seed 1019, its 0.9531041725072664 is below information-selected ridge's 0.9533160599665489. Report this local reversal and avoid blanket or significant-superiority claims over all baselines.

Budget evidence is descriptive: retain existing studied-method checkpoint values as an appendix table, with actual budget labels taken from the frozen final plan. No per-budget baseline series, fixed-target scores, tolerance-defined sufficient-k result, new inference-cost measurements, or missingness-sweep results are available.

figure_plan: Figure 1, early overview: sparse historical score matrix -> masked factor fit -> budgeted query set and purchased values -> remaining-score reconstruction, with distinct arrows showing that values update predictions but not selection; a small footer names the two source domains and two split regimes without numerical pseudo-results.

Figure 2, main comparison: four horizontal dot-plot panels, arranged by source and split, compare all six evaluated methods using actual/nonreplay case scores; display three seed points and a clearly distinguished mean per method.
Figure 3, dependence control: two source panels compare actual versus column-deranged historical training in each split using paired seed observations; use no training-time or search-trajectory axis.

planned_subsections.heading: Masked Factor Estimation and Conditional Querying
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Expand the inspected source into the masked squared-error/ridge objective, fixed column means, zero-filled centered initialization, alternating ridge updates, historical-cell rank selection, conditional prediction, and exact acquisition proxy. Explain that selection ignores observed values and includes the candidate coordinate in its current-target trace proxy. An algebraic rank-one covariance identity may explain the implementation; do not invent a recovery, optimality, or MAE guarantee. Use the staged source as implementation provenance, not as measured evidence of superiority.

planned_subsections.heading: Pinned Data Extraction, Grouping, and Reproduction
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Document the already-staged audit, plan, task contract, environment requirements, exact public source revisions, score extraction and bounds, deduplication, historical-only feature construction, heuristic name-family links, and checkpoint budgets. Preserve MTEB versus generative-model distinctions and the undeclared Open LLM dataset-license limitation. Provide exact rerun and table/figure-generation commands from the available implementation; do not invent scripts, measured storage, or timings. Treat audit/plan metadata as protocol provenance and register its evidence linkage before claiming any extra numerical dataset counts.

planned_subsections.heading: Complete Seed, Split, and Budget Tables
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Tabulate every nonreplay actual and control case, all five available baseline scores, and the studied method's retained checkpoint arrays. Map checkpoint positions to the frozen plan; do not infer absent per-budget baseline values. Include the local information-selected-ridge reversal. Mark seed variation as observed variation, not an independent-sample confidence interval, and state that missing cells were not prediction targets.

planned_subsections.heading: Aggregation, Uncertainty, and Evaluation Boundaries
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Explain equal aggregation weights and the supplied paired family-clustered bootstrap interval against random-query low-rank prediction, using the fixed plan's resampling definition. Retain the supplied interval rather than recomputing it from seed means. Describe remaining-target policy differences, absence of fixed-target controls, heuristic family labels, observational missingness, historical-cell rather than nested family validation, and lack of uncertainty for other baseline contrasts. Separate execution/replay checks from broader scientific validity.

planned_subsections.heading: Unmeasured Alternatives and Evaluation Provenance
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Briefly disclose that the retained source was the original baseline, no search-score change was measured, and all alternative attempts lack scores. Their recorded execution failures have unknown causes and do not establish inferiority or a diagnosed validity/adaptivity defect. Preserve independent final completion/qualification facts and distinguish search from final evaluation; keep machine field names and local paths out of reader-facing prose. Do not create an alternative-method leaderboard.

planned_subsections.heading: LLM Usage
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Disclose the documented role of LLM agents in alternative-method ideation/implementation and this framing/writing workflow. Distinguish unscored generated alternatives from evaluated retained code; do not assert that an LLM trained the evaluated models, ran unrecorded experiments, or independently verified literature. The writing-stage author must add its actual role without inventing undocumented human supervision.

The template is single-column: column width and full text width are both 5.5in, not a two-column 0.48-textwidth convention. Use ordinary figure environments at the planned full width. Text height is 9in. The supplied paper.tex scaffold has an identifying author and final-copy command: the future writer must anonymize it and use review formatting as required by VENUE.md, preserve the orchestrator watermark, and not claim the locally staged style has been independently verified as the latest official release.

Report the objective exactly: clip predictions to [0,1], score only available unpurchased entries, and average absolute errors within each model before the frozen hierarchy. High scores are not classification accuracy, percent of benchmarks recovered, calibrated uncertainty, or explained variance. Querying changes the target set; observed objectives cannot establish error reduction on an identical held-out panel.

A mechanistic account may derive the implemented conditional covariance/ridge equations under a working linear model. Explicitly distinguish the acquisition trace proxy from MAE optimality and from a pure off-diagonal target-risk criterion. The studied selector is sequential but does not depend on purchased score values. Do not attribute it to the unscored overlap-shrunk, latent-mixture, or monotone-skill proposals.

No new ablations, fixed-target evaluations, family-validation results, nonlinear wins, rank-sensitivity sweeps, calibration curves, real benchmark execution savings, GPU comparisons, or universal k thresholds may be planned as completed evidence. Budget tables answer only what the retained checkpoint scores show; no error-tolerance target was prespecified.

The supplied paired interval supports only the pooled comparison with random-query low-rank prediction under the observed objective. For all other comparisons use observed-score language and display seed variability without inventing p-values or confidence intervals. Do not count replay as a fourth seed or assume three seeds are independent model families.

Historical derangement preserves marginal/missingness structure while disrupting row correspondence; a score drop supports use of cross-benchmark alignment, not proof of a unique mechanism, generalization to arbitrary models, or an exhaustive validity audit. Family links are naming heuristics; MTEB and Open LLM are independent source-specific fits.

Keep all central comparisons, the actual-versus-deranged control, and essential caveats in the main text. Route full case/checkpoint tables, expanded equations, acquisition/environment details and documented unmeasured alternatives after references under Supplementary Information. Any later authoritative appendix ranking may add material there without changing this strategy.
